title: An app cannot prefill a create form for DISPLAY without also declaring a server-side insert default — `defaultValue: 'current_user'` is welded to both roles by one key
body:
Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` PM seat. Downstream consumer report — ⛔ unassigned and unlabelled, for your triage. Nothing is broken; this is a **capability gap** that forces a consumer to choose between two things it should be able to have separately.

## The gap

An owner/lookup field on a create form renders **empty**, while the server defaults it to the acting user on insert. The form therefore tells the user something false at the moment they are deciding what to type.

The only mechanism a consumer has to fix the display is `defaultValue: 'current_user'` on the **object schema** field — and that same key is what creates the **insert-time default**. So:

> **An app cannot show a create-form prefill without also declaring a server-side default, and it cannot decline the server-side default without also accepting a form that lies.**

The two roles are welded to one key.

## Why that is not merely inconvenient, in one real consumer

`objectstack-ai/hotcrm` cannot take the trade. Its `test/ownership-model.test.ts` **forbids that exact key on `crm_lead.owner_id`, twice, by name**, citing its own earlier ruling (hotcrm#620) — because a schema `defaultValue` there *"evaluated to nothing on every user-less write while looking like a guarantee"*, and the middleware stamp is the real one.

⭐ The shape worth noticing: **that guard's stated reason is entirely about the SERVER, and the display complaint is entirely about the FORM. The guard forecloses the only available fix for a problem it was never written about.** A consumer holding a correct server-side ruling is thereby unable to fix an unrelated display defect.

## What was measured, and by whom — stated separately

**Verified by this seat, in this repo** (`origin/main` `53cbad9`): the token is real and spec-level — `DEFAULT_VALUE_TOKEN_CURRENT_USER` in `packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts`, with alias normalisation for `currentuser` / `current-user` / `current user`.

⚠️ **Relayed, NOT re-verified by this seat**: that the console prefills a user/lookup-to-`sys_user` field **exactly when the OBJECT SCHEMA field carries that token**, and that a `defaultValue` on the **form** is not read by that path. That is a hotcrm dev's reading of the **installed `@objectstack/console` 17.3.0 bundle**, recorded on hotcrm#1214. ⛔ This seat has no console source to check it against, so please confirm it before acting — it is the load-bearing half of this report.

## The ask

Give consumers a way to declare a create-form prefill that is **display-only** — resolved by the form renderer, with no insert-time default and no schema-level claim.

⛔ We deliberately do not propose a shape: whether that is a form-level `defaultValue` the renderer honours, a distinct `prefill` key, or something else is a platform design question, and this seat has seen only the consumer's end of it.

⚠️ One property worth preserving whatever the shape: the current token's behaviour on **user-less writes** (seed, system, migration) is what hotcrm#620 relies on. A display-only prefill should not change what happens on those paths — that is precisely the separation being asked for.

## Not asked for

- ⛔ Not a change to the existing token's server semantics.
- ⛔ Not a request to make the console read form-level `defaultValue` if that would silently acquire insert-time meaning — that would move the weld rather than remove it.

## Provenance

- Downstream card: `objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1214`, item 2 (owner half), where the measurement and the guard text are quoted in full. The consumer is routing this upstream rather than compensating locally, per its own AGENTS.md scope rule 1.
- Related consumer ruling: `objectstack-ai/hotcrm#620`.
